name: Hill paddy plot on a Sarawak slope
headline: Traditional hill rice on cleared slopes: food security for the family, but bare soil under the heaviest rains in Malaysia.
story: A 1.5 ha hillside plot farmed by a Bidayuh family, planted to traditional hill rice once a year from about September and then left to bush fallow. Yields are under 2 t/ha, the cleared slope is bare when the northeast monsoon rains peak, and fallow periods have shrunk as land gets scarce.

baseline_rotation.name: Hill rice, then bush fallow
baseline_rotation.note: Sentinel-2 shows a single crop cycle in alternate years with regrowth between; hill rice is the customary crop.

water_context.note: No irrigation. Rain is abundant (over 3,500 mm) but dry spells of two to three weeks in June-August still hurt hill rice at flowering.

hill_rice.note: Mostly eaten at home; Bario-type and heritage varieties sell at a premium in Kuching.
